flagged_questions.en: And that Rākṣasa of dreadful form daily frightens people. And, O descendant of Raghu, Tātakā of wicked deeds, daily commits havoc upon these countries, Maladã and Karuşă.

flagged_questions.en: All the monkeys are depressed. O Hanuman, did you overlook this? Put forth your you endowed with mighty vehemence, like Vişnu sing over the three worlds in three steps.

flagged_questions.question: How does this teaching spoken to Rama compare family, home, and property to a traveler's overnight stop?
flagged_questions.flag_notes: Question keeps the triad parents/home/wealth and the traveler-lodging analogy, which is the verse's distinctive wording.
flagged_questions.en: No individual has any one (in the world). As on the eve of setting out for another country, a person stays somewhere (outside the village he lives in), and the next day goes away, renouncing that abode, even such are a man's father and mother, house and wealth. O Kākutstha, worthy people never bear affection towards a mere abode.

flagged_questions.question: How did Duryodhana propose to buy Drupada's court away from Yudhishthira's side?
flagged_questions.flag_notes: Same Duryodhana-Vidura plotting conversation as the Dhritarashtra/Vidura-concealment question (row 25737).
flagged_questions.en: Or let the king Drupada with his sons and ail his ministers of state be tempted by the presents of large wealth, so that they may abandon the cause of the son of Kunti, Yudhishthira. Or let them (our spies) speak to each of them separately the inconvenience of this place (Hastinapur) and induce them to live there (in Panchala.) Thus separated from the Kurus, they may live permanently there.

flagged_questions.question: In Krishna's battlefield teaching to Arjuna, what kind of person is said to attain peace?
flagged_questions.flag_notes: Related Gita cluster with the egoism/killing teaching (row 48559).
flagged_questions.en: The man, who moves about casting of all desires, and being freed from attachments, carvings for things, and egoism (pride), attains to peace.

flagged_questions.question: When the Pandavas consulted after the ninth day's fight, what did they recall Bhishma had promised about counsel versus fighting?
flagged_questions.flag_notes: 51531 is a continuation of the same quoted pledge. Review whether it independently answers or is only the next clause.
flagged_questions.en: Before this battle there was an understanding between me and Bhishma. He said 'I will give you good counsel, but will not fight for your interests.

flagged_questions.question: During the fight at Saubha, what did Krishna say he started doing with his arrows to the enemies of the gods?
flagged_questions.flag_notes: Same Saubha episode as the question about where Shalva stood (row 29690).
flagged_questions.en: Krishna said : O best of the Bharata race, then taking up my beautiful bow, I began to cut off with my arrows the heads of the enemies of the celestials from the (car) Saubha.

flagged_questions.question: On that morning of battle, which Kaurava leaders did Shikhandin attack with Virata, and which leaders did Arjuna attack?
flagged_questions.flag_notes: Battle-cluster overlap with other Kurukshetra action questions.
flagged_questions.en: Sanjaya said O ruler of men, Shikhandin, with the king of the Matsyas viz., Virata, speedily rushed against Bhishma, that mighty bowman difficult of being defeated in battle. Dhananjaya in that battle rushed against Drona, Kripa, Vikarna, and many kings, all mighty-bowmen, brave,, and endued with great prowess.

flagged_questions.question: Why was Dhritarashtra told not to grieve for the slain Kuru heroes?
flagged_questions.flag_notes: Related 'why grieve' cluster with Arjuna's later speeches to Yudhishthira (rows 70460, 70066).
flagged_questions.en: This destruction of the Kurus, O king, was inevitable. Why then do you grieve for those heroes that have achieved the highest end?

flagged_questions.question: After Yudhishthira had won the kingdom by Kshatriya duty, why did Arjuna ask him not to keep grieving?
flagged_questions.flag_notes: Same Rajadharmanushasana consolation cluster as row 70066.
flagged_questions.en: 'O you who are conversant with every kind of duty, having by the practise of Kshatriya duties acquired sovereignty that is so very difficult of acquisition, and having defeated all your foes, why do you grieve.

flagged_questions.question: According to this teaching, why do ascetics regarded as wise refuse meat as food?
flagged_questions.flag_notes: The verse announces the faults but does not list them. Review whether announcing the reason to refrain is enough of an answer.
flagged_questions.en: It is therefore, that wise men who are gifted with penances refrain from eating meat. Listen to me, O king, as tell you what the faults are which attach to the eating of meat.

flagged_questions.question: In this enumeration of foremost beings, who rules the waters, the storm-gods, hot bodies, and luminous bodies?
flagged_questions.flag_notes: Indra appears twice (Maruts and luminous bodies). Review whether the last item is Indra or Indu/moon; Dutt prints 'Indra of all luminous bodies' while the Sanskrit has indu.
flagged_questions.en: Varuna is the king of the waters. Indra is said to be the king of the Maruts. Arka is the king of all hot bodies, and Indra of all luminous bodies.

flagged_questions.question: After the dice-game injuries, why did the speaker say the Pandavas would not forgive the Kauravas?
flagged_questions.flag_notes: Dice-game aftermath cluster with the elders' 'Fie' reaction (pilot_03) and Dhrishtadyumna's killer list (pilot_06). Different questions, same broader episode.
flagged_questions.en: Persecuted (as) they are (by us), they cannot forgive us for those injuries. Who is there amongst them who will be able to forgive the insult to Draupadi?

flagged_questions.question: What spiritual result is promised to people who tell Vyasa's history to others, or who listen to it?
flagged_questions.flag_notes: Meta-textual claim about the Mahabharata itself rather than a story event. Review whether this is an appropriate realistic user question.
flagged_questions.en: The Brahmanas who recite it for others to hear it and those who hear it, in whatever state duties, they may be, can never be affected by the fruits of good or bad deeds.

flagged_questions.question: According to this Gita teaching, what is said of a person without egoism whose mind is unsullied, even if he kills many people?
flagged_questions.flag_notes: Related Gita cluster with the peace-through-renouncing-desire teaching (row 48051).
flagged_questions.en: He who has no egoism, and whose mind is not sullied, does not kill, or fettered by action, if he kills all these people.

flagged_questions.question: According to Sanjaya, what was Bhishma trying to protect by fighting so hard that morning?
flagged_questions.flag_notes: Kurukshetra battle cluster with other Bhishma-fight questions.
flagged_questions.en: Sanjaya said Then Bhishma, the son of Shantanu, fought a fierce battle, desirous of saving your sons from their fear of Bhimasena. In that morning, a most dreadful battle was fought between the kings of the Kaurava and the Pandava hosts, in which many best warriors were slain.

flagged_questions.question: At the trial of arms, how did the spectators react to Duryodhana's speech, and what happened in the sky afterward?
flagged_questions.flag_notes: Thin unique fact (cheers plus sunset). Review whether this is too weak for the benchmark.
flagged_questions.en: Thereupon there arose a loud cheer among all the spectators, approving of Duryodhana's speech. At this time the sun went down.

flagged_questions.question: What did Abhimanyu do when he saw Dhrishtadyumna engaged with Ashvatthaman?
flagged_questions.flag_notes: Generic battle-action verse; review distinctiveness.
flagged_questions.en: O descendant of Bharata, seeing Dhrishtadyumna fighting with Drona's son, the son of Subhadra (Abhimanyu) ran up showering his fearful arrows.

flagged_questions.question: What sounds from Drona's pavilion did Dhritarashtra say he used to hear constantly but could no longer hear?
flagged_questions.flag_notes: English is garbled ('were the be heard'). Neighboring verses also say other camps' sounds are gone; gold is limited to Drona's pavilion only.
flagged_questions.en: The twang of bows, the sound of Vedic recitations, the whistle of shafts, the whiz of swords and the rattle of cars, these sounds were the be heard incessantly in the pavilion of Drona. But I do not hear them now.

flagged_questions.question: When Arjuna saw the Samsaptakas formed against him, how did he respond?
flagged_questions.flag_notes: Generic battle-action verse.
flagged_questions.en: Beholding he Samsaptakas in battle array, Arjuna, worked up with anger, rushed against them, drawing his Gandiva bow.

flagged_questions.question: After conquering the earth, what did Arjuna say it was foolish for a royal-born king like Yudhishthira to do?

flagged_questions.en: You are born in a royal family. Having conquered the whole Earth, do you foolishly wish to live in the forest after for-saking everything of virtue of profit?

flagged_questions.question: Why, in Dhritarashtra's lament, would a man who had already reached heaven in his own body come back to earth?

flagged_questions.en: What man is there who having gone to heaven in his own human body ever wishes to come back? Because he sees the Kurus at the point of death by Time, he has returned.

flagged_questions.question: According to this account of Duryodhana as a portion of Kali, what role did he play in starting the great destruction?

flagged_questions.question: Where was this cosmic being said to have been born, and for what purpose in the world?
flagged_questions.flag_notes: The verse does not name Krishna in this row; the identification is from context. Review whether the question should name Krishna or leave it as 'this great being'.
flagged_questions.en: This great being, possessed of infinite wealth, this Grandsire of all creatures, took his birth in the race of Andhaka Vrishnis, in order to increase the piety in the world.

flagged_questions.question: What did Dhritarashtra tell Duryodhana about revealing his thoughts to Vidura?
flagged_questions.flag_notes: Same plotting conversation as the Drupada-bribe question (row 25741).
flagged_questions.en: Dhritarashtra said : I desire to act exactly as you desire, but I do not wish to show my mental thoughts to Vidura even by my demeanour.

flagged_questions.question: When people followed Yudhishthira into exile out of grief, what did he tell them to do?
flagged_questions.flag_notes: Source English is broken ('Go back. heart be...'). Same forest-departure cluster as the farewell question (row 28889).
flagged_questions.en: Grieved at my departure, you have come far away. Go back. heart be affectionately directed towards the relatives whom we leave behind as our pledges to you.

flagged_questions.question: Where did Krishna say he found Shalva standing with the Saubha car?
flagged_questions.flag_notes: Same Saubha episode as Krishna cutting off heads (row 29736).
flagged_questions.en: O slayer of foes, having reached the ocean (I saw) Shalva on his (Saubha, car made of precious metal in the midst of the ocean full of heaving billows.

flagged_questions.question: After Pushkara cheated Nala at dice, where did Nala go to live, and who went with him?
flagged_questions.flag_notes: Nala cluster with the later dice-or-duel question (row 31560). Different moments.
flagged_questions.en: We have heard that the king was deceitfully defeated by Pushkara; and in consequence defeated by Pushkara; and in consequence thereof he dwelt in the forest with his spouse, pressed with distress.

flagged_questions.question: At the opening of the Mahabharata, what did Dhritarashtra tell Sanjaya about his own attitude toward war and the destruction of his race?
flagged_questions.flag_notes: Anukramanika framing speech rather than an in-story event verse. Review suitability.
flagged_questions.en: You are learned in the Shastras, you are intelligent and you are possessed of wisdom. (Hear), my inclinations were never for war, nor did I feel pleasure in the destruction of my race.
